\[
n(r_0) = \sum_{\lvert r - r_0 \rvert \le 3.4} e^{-\left(\frac{I(r) - I(r_0)}{t}\right)^6},
\qquad
R(r_0) = \begin{cases} g - n(r_0) & n(r_0) < g \\ 0 & \text{otherwise} \end{cases},
\qquad
t = 25,\ g = 0.75 \cdot 37
\]

The formula shows the default parameter values.

where

- \(r_0\): The nucleus, the center pixel
- \(n\): The USAN area
- \(t\): The brightness threshold
- \(g\): The geometric threshold
- \(R\): The edge response

The mask is a circle of 37 pixels around the nucleus r_0. Each pixel counts as similar by a smooth step of the brightness difference, and n, the USAN area, adds them up. USAN stands for univalue segment assimilating nucleus. In a flat area n is 37. On a straight edge it is about half. The edge response R grows as n falls below the geometric threshold g. The paper sets g to three quarters of 37 to reject noise. The edge direction comes from the USAN: the vector from the nucleus to its center of gravity crosses the edge. Where the USAN is a thin line, its longest axis runs along the edge. Non-maximum suppression across the edge then thins it.
